newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cavallo retracts graft comments on Argentine judge.
newsitem.headline: Cavallo retracts graft comments on Argentine judge.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, facing court action left, right and center for his outspoken denunciations of official corruption, apologized to a Supreme Court judge Monday for such charges.

Cavallo is abroad, but his lawyers filed a retraction that admitted he made the comments about Judge Augusto Belluscio "without personally checking the quality of the information I had and whether it was complete and accurate."

The case dates back to 1993, when Cavallo called Belluscio and High Court colleague Enrique Petracchi "corrupt thieves" because of their ruling in a case against the Central Bank. Both sued, but Petracchi accepted a retraction last month.
Belluscio's lawyer Eduardo Zanoni told local radio Monday that his client wanted "a straightforward retraction without conditions."

Cavallo was sacked three months ago after doing a widely praised job as economy minister. He beat hyperinflation and fostered growth with his 1991 Convertibility Plan pegging the peso to the dollar and managed the sale of state enterprises.

The Harvard-trained economist has whipped up a political storm since his sacking by continuing his personal crusade aginst official corruption with accusations against two ministers and President Carlos Menem's top aide.
They deny the charges and are threatening legal action, while another Argentine judge is fighting Cavallo in court over corruption allegations.
Cavallo, asked recently in Brazil whether he plans to run for president in 1999, answered with defiant humor: "I don't think I'll be president because they'll put me in jail first."
Clarin newspaper quoted Cavallo's legal aides saying his retraction to the High Court judge was aimed at "reducing his exposure in the courts" to avoid such a fate.
